description:
Create `src/extractor/fsharp/` with the F# console app that uses FSharp.Compiler.Service.

Layout
- `src/extractor/fsharp/Catseye.FSharp.Extractor.fsproj` — net8.0 (or as decided in spike), references `FSharp.Compiler.Service` from nuget.
- `src/extractor/fsharp/Program.fs` — entry point. CLI: `catseye-fsharp-extractor <file.fs|fsx|fsi> [--out <path>]`. Default: write to stdout.
- `src/extractor/fsharp/AstEmitter.fs` — walks `FSharpAst`, emits the wire format decided in catseye-9mh.1. Encapsulate the XML element naming + attribute conventions so they're documented in one place.
- `src/extractor/fsharp/Symbols.fs` — pulls the typed symbols we care about (function names, parameter names, type names) from `FSharpChecker.GetBackgroundCheckResultsForFile` so the mapper can record them.
- `src/extractor/fsharp/README.md` — short: what it does, how to build (`dotnet build`), how to invoke, where the wire-format spec lives.
- `.gitignore` entries for `bin/`, `obj/`, `*.user`.

Constraints
- Must compile on a clean `nix develop` shell (depends on catseye-9mh.2).
- Exit codes: 0 on success, 2 on parse error, 1 on I/O. Errors go to stderr with file:line:col when FCS provides them.
- No silent fallbacks — if the file won't parse, return non-zero so the OCaml side can fall back gracefully (or skip).
- Avoid `dotnet new`-generated boilerplate cruft (telemetry, launch profiles, etc.) — keep the project minimal.

Acceptance
- `dotnet build` succeeds.
- `dotnet run -- /path/to/valid.fs` emits the wire format agreed in the spike.
- `dotnet run -- /nonexistent.fs` exits non-zero with a clear error.
- Output of one real F# file is checked into `tests/fixtures/fsharp/spike-output.xml` (coord with spike ticket).

Blocked by: catseye-9mh.1, catseye-9mh.2.
Worktree: `catseye-9mh.3/fsharp-extractor-scaffold`.
